test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How long can a person remain a minister without being a member of either House of the State Legislature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 months**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A person can remain a minister without being a member of either House of the State Legislature for a maximum period of **6 months**.
 
• This provision allows an individual to be appointed as a minister and subsequently seek election to either House of the State Legislature within this time frame.
 
• If the individual is not elected within 6 months, they must step down from their ministerial position.
 
• This rule ensures that the executive branch remains accountable to the legislative branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This provision is outlined in **Article 164(4) **of the Constitution of India.
 
• The intent behind this provision is to provide flexibility in the appointment of ministers while ensuring democratic legitimacy through eventual election.
 
• Similar provisions exist for the Union government under **Article 75(5)** of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India aims to balance the need for experienced and capable ministers with the imperative of democratic accountability.
